title: Why Stream ring-maker Sandbar says the future of AI wearables is voice
slides: Who will win the AI wearable war?
Sandbar's new ring skips screens entirely.
Users now talk to devices, not tap them.
Tomorrow, test voice-first commands on your phone.
thread_text:
1. Who's Next?

Sandbar’s ring ditches screens completely, betting voice-first is the future.

2. 3x Faster

Voice-only beats touch in speed by 3x. Users are already talking, not tapping.

3. Tap to Talk

Rings are the new wearables, and they're all about conversation.

4. The Shift

Devices now listen, not just display. Your wrist is becoming your assistant.

5. Try It Today

Test voice commands on your phone tomorrow. Notice how it feels.

instagram.caption:
Your next wearable might not have a screen at all. 🔊

Sandbar's new ring is voice-only, and they say talking beats tapping by 3x in speed. No display, no menus—just commands.

The shift: devices are starting to listen instead of showing. For anyone creating content, that means thinking in voice-first phrases, not visual steps.

Do you already dictate more than you type? Try one voice command on your phone today and see if it actually feels faster. 🎙️⌚

carousel_slides.description: Sandbar's ring skips screens entirely, betting on voice-first. Could this redefine how we interact with wearables and win the AI wearable war?
Voice-only interaction outperforms touch in speed, a 3x advantage. Users are already switching from tapping to talking for faster, more natural commands.

carousel_slides.hook: Talk to your ring, not tap
carousel_slides.description: Sandbar's ring is all about conversation. It listens to your voice, not your fingers, making interactions more intuitive and hands-free.
The shift is real: devices now listen to you, not just show screens. Your wrist is becoming an active assistant that responds to your voice.
Test voice commands on your phone tomorrow. Notice how it feels—faster? More natural? Share your experience in the comments!
